doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: What swing is, and playing Sing Sing Sing
summary: Fillius defines the swing beat, praises Butch Miles, and recalls playing drums to records to relieve tension in San Diego.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Right. I’ve asked a number of the musicians what is swing.
Do you have an idea on how to define that?

Yeah. It has a beat. There’s no other beat like it. And there are people who played in the swing era who weren’t swingers, but the minute I hear it I know it. The beat. It’s a heavy four/four beat, and — it’s heavy but it’s light at the same time. It’s totally unlike the rock & roll stuff with the drummer banging away. I mean that doesn’t take any talent to do that. But you see if a fellow like Butch, Butch Miles. He’s the epitome of a good swing drummer. Now all you have to do is listen to him make rhythm and that’s it. And everybody reacts to it, the swing people.
Did you learn any of that swing drumming from your teacher at Eastman?
Oh no, no, just the rudiments.
Right. So after that it was pretty much listening and emulating?

Yeah. Well I used to do “Sing Sing Sing” with my eyes closed. In fact, later on in life when I was running a shipyard in San Diego, I had a big house and one room was a music room and I had in it huge speakers and my drumset. And I would come home from work tense and ready to kill somebody you know, and I’d turn on a record and play it as loud as I could and I’d go in and beat the drums and play with it. And that was the way I relieved tension in those days. But it’s very distinctive. It’s a rhythm and it’s catchy. It lilts. And the minute you put something on I can tell whether it’s swing music or not. But that rhythm is still — well when you hear all the concerts we’ve got, they’ve all been swing based. I don’t’ know that that’s the right word for it or the right term, but that’s where it started.
